claim: Against control on the identical detection stream, dedup_hours=48 raises net EV per trade and does not lower win rate, while max drawdown falls because same-name stacked positions disappear; it will cut sample volume, so if EV per trade is flat or lower, or drawdown is unchanged, the concentration mechanism is false and the arm dies.
why: REFUTED_BEFORE: matches G-06 via 'cascade' — Cluster / cascade filter (isolated pumps better) (Live isolated 65% vs cascade 38% (p=.047 on 7d). Honest 249d: 56.1% vs 57.1% — and 11+ clusters were actually best.)

claim: dedup_hours=24 moves net EV per trade up and max drawdown down versus control on the shared detection stream, with win rate flat or better and a materially smaller sample loss than the 48h cap; if the 48h arm shows an effect and this one does not, the harmful correlation extends beyond one day and the 24h framing is wrong.
why: history: This project has already run this experiment twice under different names. G-10 (re-pump recency) tested exactly the population dedup_hours=24 would remove: a coin that fired 6-48h ago. The live signal at p=.066 went flat at p=.58 on honest data. A 24h cap is precisely a rule that deletes those 6-48h repeat fills, so G-10 says the deleted trades are statistically indistinguishable from the ones kept — dropping them cannot move net EV per trade, it only shrinks n. G-06 (cluster/cascade filter) is the same causal claim one level up: 'one distribution campaign should contribute one trade, not several correlated ones' IS 'isolated pumps beat cascades'. Honest 249d gave 56.1% isolated vs 57.1% cascade, and 11+ clusters were the BEST bucket — the correlation the proposal calls harmful was measured and found mildly beneficial. G-14 adds the third strike: split-half WR correlation by coin r = -0.002, so same-name stacking carries no persistent penalty to remove. The proposal's own framing concedes the weak form of this: it argues 24h over 48h purely on sample preservation, i.e. it is optimising power for an effect whose existence was already refuted at p=.58. The 0.12% slippage haircut is charged per extra fill on both sides of the comparison and does not create a per-trade EV lift from deletion; a filter that removes average-EV trades is a volume dial, the same trap as G-08. Blocking terms 're-pump', 'recent pump same coin', 'cluster filter', 'isolated pump' all fire.; mechanism: The mechanism is not a reason, it is a re-description of a pattern already refuted. Dedup is already ON at dedup_hours=6, and detection uses pump_window_h<=6, so 'one campaign contributes one trade' is satisfied by the incumbent. The only population 6->24 actually removes is the second fill in a coin that pumped again 6-24h later — which is exactly G-10 (re-pump recency, 6-48h band), where a live p=.066 went flat at p=.58 on honest data, and adjacent to G-06 where isolated-vs-cascade collapsed to 56.1% vs 57.1% with 11+ clusters best. The proposal offers no reason those second fills are worse trades; 'correlated' is a variance/portfolio property, not a per-trade EV property, so the stated cause cannot produce the predicted move in EV or WR. It equally predicts the opposite: a coin re-pumping into an already-stretched move is a higher short entry, and G-26 found uptrend pumps short BETTER, so removing the second leg should lower per-trade EV. The one channel that does move the number is accounting, not edge — deleting the fills that pay the 0.12% extra-fill haircut raises mean EV/trade while cutting total PnL, the same volume-for-a-dial trade that killed G-08 (ACC/XC). The 24h boundary is set by convenience ('calendar-day'), not by any measured campaign life in this context; hold-12h implies a 12h trade life, so 24h is unmotivated. The falsification clause references a '48h cap' arm that does not exist in the arena, making the stated test unfalsifiable as written, and the class label 'universe' is wrong — dedup_hours changes no coin's eligibility, it is a timing/entry_trigger dial.; statistics: The proposal's own framing concedes it is a sample-preserving variant, which means the trades it actually changes are only the repeat fills inside a 24h window — a small subset of the shared detection stream, so the arm's screen population will be nearly identical to control (screen_n=1534, screen_wr=49.739, screen_ev=0.016) and the delta it can register is correspondingly tiny. The context supplies no count of within-24h repeat detections, so there is no number here establishing that the changed-trade subset is large enough to move EV at all; by the stated rule that a fixed n=100 detects only very large effects and small ideas need the full planned n=600, an effect concentrated in a thin slice of fills cannot clear corrected alpha 0.00833. Worse, that slice is structurally confounded: repeat fills within a day cluster in whichever few coins pumped repeatedly and in whatever regime the 60.7-day window happened to contain (176 coins, 246445 candles, live tier only n=19), which is precisely the PM/SN/MT pattern that killed G-10 re-pump recency (live p=.066 to flat p=.58) and G-14 coin persistence (r=-0.002). The hypothesis is also unfalsifiable as written — it pre-commits to reinterpreting a null as evidence about the 48h arm, which is max-of-k reasoning across two correlated dedup arms against a lifetime budget already at 6 tests. Finally, the EV case rests on saving the 0.12% haircut on extra fills, but removing fills also removes their wins, and no number in this context shows repeat fills are worse than first fills.

claim: Against control on the identical detection stream, dedup_hours=2 raises sample volume and delivers net EV per trade at least equal to control with win rate flat or better and max drawdown unchanged; if the restored second-leg fills come in below control EV by more than the 0.12% slippage haircut charged on extra fills, or if max drawdown rises from same-name overlap, the second-leg exhaustion mechanism is false and the arm dies.
why: history: This project has already measured the exact population dedup_hours=2 would restore, twice, and found it carries no signal — and the proposal itself cites that finding as support, which is the tell. G-06 (cluster/cascade) honestly re-measured stacked versus isolated pumps at 57.1% vs 56.1% — flat, i.e. the second-leg population is neither better nor worse than the baseline. G-10 (re-pump recency) tested a coin firing again 6-48h after a prior pump and went from p=.066 live to flat at p=.58 on honest data. The 2-6h band this arm re-admits is the immediate continuation of that same tested band under an identical mechanism claim ('a second leg on the same name is a fresh set of buyers on a thinner book'), and nothing in the record suggests the 2-6h slice behaves differently from the 6-48h slice that was already refuted. That is the fatal asymmetry: a flat-EV population added to control cannot raise win rate or EV per trade — the fixed objective — and once the 0.12% slippage haircut is charged on every extra fill, a flat population becomes a strictly negative one. The hypothesis's own success criterion ('EV at least equal to control, volume up') is a volume criterion wearing an EV criterion's clothes, which is precisely the trap G-08 named when it found the pump floor was 'a WR dial only, and it pays volume.' Note also that L-dedup-24h and L-dedup-48h were killed on the grounds that same-name correlation structure carries no exploitable signal; if that verdict stands, it forbids moving the dial in either direction, and this arm is the same dead question with the sign flipped. The one genuinely novel element — that dedup_hours=6 exceeding pump_window_h=2 is an arbitrary mismatch — is a fair observation about parameter hygiene, but it is an argument that the discarded population is not losing, not evidence that it is winning, and only a winning population advances the objective.; mechanism: The stated reason is two disconnected claims wearing one coat, and neither is a mechanism for the objective. (1) The parameter-arithmetic part — 'the cooldown is 3x the lookback, so set it equal' — is a tidiness argument, not a causal one. Nothing about pump_window_h=2 makes 2 the correct suppression length. The timescale that governs same-name overlap is the holding period, and max_hold_h=24: at dedup_hours=2 a fresh detection fires up to eleven more times while the first position is still open, all driven by one underlying move, with sl_anchor=peak re-anchoring the stop to each new higher peak. The proposal asserts 'max drawdown unchanged' but supplies no reason for it, while its own parameter change is a direct generator of correlated same-name stacking — the constraint it must not violate. (2) The economic part — 'a thinner book already holding trapped longs' — predicts the opposite outcome just as well as the stated one. Trapped longs from leg one are the fuel that produced the dump the first short already harvested; if they were flushed, leg two has FEWER of them, not more. And a thinner book is equally a book that is cheaper to push UP, which under a peak-anchored stop is a stop-out, not an exhaustion. The story contains no term that selects continuation from reversal, so it is a pattern description ('second legs feel exhausted') rather than a reason. That is the exact MECH failure that put the graveyard where it is. (3) The supporting citation is a population mismatch: G-06's honest 57.1% vs 56.1% was measured on trades that had already survived dedup_hours=6, so it says nothing about the same-name-within-6h population this arm would restore — it cannot license that population being non-losing. The nearest honest measurement of the actual claim, G-10's re-pump recency, went flat at p=.58, i.e. a coin that fired recently is not in a distinguishable state. (4) Fatally, the hypothesis's own success condition is parity: 'net EV per trade at least equal to control'. Control screen_ev=0.029 on n=1541, and the extra fills are charged a 0.12% slippage haircut — four times control EV. So the restored second legs must clear control by more than 0.12%/trade just to leave total EV where it is, while the mechanism only ever claims they are 'not a losing population'. A mechanism whose best-case prediction is indistinguishable from the null, on an objective that is per-trade EV and win rate rather than volume, is not a mechanism for this objective at all. It is the volume side of the same dial G-08 died on.; statistics: Statistically this arm cannot produce an informative verdict. (1) The comparison is paired on an identical detection stream, so every trade control also takes contributes zero discordance — the entire signal lives in the incremental second-leg fills alone. Nothing in this context states how many such fills exist; the only other dedup arms ever run (dedup-24h, dedup-48h) reached screen_n=0. If the extra fills are a fraction f of the blended sample, the arm's effective sample for the question asked is f*n, not n, and the confirm plan of n=600 shrinks accordingly. (2) The required effect is enormous, not small. With control EV 0.029%/trade and a 0.12% slippage haircut charged on extra fills, blended EV = (1-f)(0.029) + f(e - 0.12), so the restored population must earn e >= 0.149%/trade — over five times control EV — merely to hold EV flat. Anything less is dilution, and the proposal's own hypothesis concedes it only expects 'at least equal'. (3) The supporting evidence quantifies the effect as ~1pp: the honest cluster re-measurement cited is 57.1% vs 56.1%. A 1pp win-rate difference is undetectable at corrected alpha 0.00833 with n=600 — this context already states a fixed n=100 detects only very large effects, and even sl-5pct's 5.26pp on screen_n=1540 has not cleared the bar. The arm is powered to detect an effect an order of magnitude larger than the one its own mechanism predicts. (4) Confounding is structural, not incidental: the restored population is by construction repeat firings of the SAME name within 2-6h, so extra fills cluster into a handful of coins and a handful of cluster episodes. Nominal n overstates independent information; the arm risks being decided by one or two names in one regime window. (5) The drawdown clause is untestable — max drawdown is a single extreme-order statistic per run, and 'unchanged' cannot be demonstrated at any sample this arm will reach. (6) The hypothesis is written so that a flat result passes ('EV at least equal to control, WR flat or better'), which is acceptance of the null dressed as a test: adding trades pulls blended EV toward control by arithmetic, so the arm drifts to 'pass' without evidence while consuming one of the 6 lifetime tests the corrected alpha is already paying for.

claim: With dedup_hours=0, net EV per trade is flat or higher than control on the shared detection stream and win rate does not fall, while sample volume rises well above the 25.6 control trades/day baseline so the confirm n=600 is reached faster; the arm dies if EV per trade drops below control by more than the 0.12% extra-fill slippage haircut, or if max drawdown increases because concurrent same-name positions stop out together.
why: REFUTED_BEFORE: matches G-06 via 'cascade' — Cluster / cascade filter (isolated pumps better) (Live isolated 65% vs cascade 38% (p=.047 on 7d). Honest 249d: 56.1% vs 57.1% — and 11+ clusters were actually best.)

claim: Against control on the identical detection stream, min_price=1.0 raises win rate counted by PnL sign with timeouts included, and raises net EV per trade after fees and measured slippage, with max drawdown flat or lower because the widest peak-anchored losses are concentrated in the removed coarse-grid names. It will cut sample volume below the 25.2 control trades/day arrival, so the confirm n=600 takes longer; if win rate is flat or lower than control, or net EV per trade is flat or lower, the tick-quantisation mechanism is false and the arm dies with no reprieve for slower accumulation.
why: history: This is G-13 (price level / microcap proxy, blocks='price level', 'coin price bucket') re-executed as a parameter. G-13 died because the $0.1-1 band was the WORST live and the BEST on cache — directly contradictory — so the project already has a measurement of exactly the population min_price=1.0 removes, and it has no stable sign. The proposal's defence ('the claim is about the execution grid, not which price band carries alpha') changes the story told about the cut but not the cut itself: the arm is still a nominal-price bucket boundary, and it will be scored on the same contradictory population that killed G-13. Re-running a filter that already gave opposite answers on two windows, under a new rationale, is PR/MT, not a new test. Two further rhymes make the transfer stronger, not weaker. (1) G-03 and G-09 both died on the identical structural finding: a hard threshold on a continuous coin attribute shows NO discontinuity at the boundary. A tick-geometry story predicts a smooth monotone degradation as price falls, which is precisely the shape that a step at 1.0 cannot capture and that this project has twice measured as flat. (2) G-41 is the binding one: the edge is KEPT AS A FINDING to be a thin-alt mean-reversion phenomenon (HL net EV/t +0.149% vs Binance -0.180%, 145 of 172 HL coins HL-only), and G-40 records that the validated cache result applies to ESTABLISHED coins only while the bot monitors 177 including PURR, HMSTR, XPL, MEME. A $1 floor deletes the thin-alt population the edge was located in and shifts the arm toward the established-coin population the project has already flagged as a population mismatch — so an EV move here is confounded with PM and is not attributable to tick coarseness. Finally, the mechanism's own premise is unverified in this context: nothing here reports HL tick size or measured spread by price band, only min_price, and no number in this context links nominal price to relative tick or to realised slippage beyond the flat 0.12% haircut charged on extra fills. The stated MECHANISM is therefore an assertion about a quantity the project has not measured, attached to a cut it has already measured and found contradictory.; mechanism: The stated cause is a pattern relabelled, not a reason, and it is internally self-cancelling. (1) It asserts the two halves of a bet in the same breath: a coarse tick inflates the recorded peak, so the peak-anchored stop sits mechanically WIDER — and this project's own evidence says a wider peak anchor RAISES win rate (G-34/L-sl-entry-anchor: tightening the anchor to entry took WR 79% to 60%, and the live screen kill measured WR -9.10pp on n=1474). So the first sub-mechanism predicts sub-dollar names should win MORE often, while the proposal's conclusion is that they win less. Both signs are derivable from the same premise, which means no outcome can falsify it. That is the definition of a non-mechanism. (2) The second sub-mechanism, a larger effective spread as a share of price, is a symmetric level tax on entry and exit. A constant cost shifts EV down by a constant; it does not preferentially 'convert marginal winners to stop-outs' unless the stop and target are asymmetrically placed relative to it, which is never argued. And that cost is already the thing the 0.12% measured-slippage haircut and the fee-adjusted EV accounting exist to charge — the arm changes no accounting, so it cannot claim a cost that the objective's 'net of fees and measured slippage' framing has not already priced. (3) The load-bearing premise — that tick is a large fraction of price on sub-dollar HL alts — is asserted, never measured, and no tick, spread, or quote-granularity number appears anywhere in this context. The mechanism rests on 'the recorded peak sits further above the true clearing level', where the 'true' level is unobservable by construction. For one tick to matter against a 3.0% sl_pct and 5.0% tp_pct measured in percent, a tick would have to be a material fraction of those percentages; nothing here establishes that, and HL quoting is significant-figure based, which makes relative tick size roughly price-invariant and the whole geometric story empty. (4) Strip the prose and the testable prediction is identical to G-13 (price level / microcap proxy), which died precisely because the $0.1-1 band was worst live and best on cache — directly contradictory. The proposal's disclaimer that it is 'about the execution grid, not which price band carries alpha' is a rename: the parameter moved, the population removed, and the predicted direction are all exactly G-13's, and a new story for an old prediction is the MECH failure mode this graveyard is made of. (5) It also points the wrong way on population: G-41 established the edge is a thin-alt mean-reversion phenomenon with 145 of 172 HL coins HL-only, and G-40 named PURR, HMSTR, XPL, MEME as the monitored universe outside the validated cache. A $1.00 floor deletes the cheap thin alts that are the stated carrier of the edge, so the mechanism, taken seriously, predicts the objective gets worse.; statistics: This arm carries almost no statistical information at the bar it must clear. min_price=1.0 is a pure subsetting filter: it never changes the outcome of a trade it keeps, so against control on the identical detection stream every retained trade is the same trade, discordant pairs are zero by construction, and the paired machinery that killed L-sl-entry-anchor (b=0/c=134, p=9.18e-41 on n=1474) has nothing to test. The arena confirms this: every filter-class arm in confirm reports screen_dWR=0.0pp — entry-8pct (screen_n=496), vol-4x (screen_n=866) and placebo (min_price=1e-12, screen_n=1550, wr=49.935, ev=0.034, exactly control) all read 0.0pp. The proposal is the same knob as the placebo at a binding level, and the placebo is in the arena precisely to show this dial returns control's numbers. What remains is an unpaired subset-vs-whole contrast, i.e. picking a price band and asking whether it beats the pooled rest — the max-of-k selection that G-13 already ran, where $0.1-1 was worst live and best on cache, contradictory in sign, meaning any true price-band effect is smaller than the sampling noise of the samples available here. Accrual makes it worse. Control arrives at 25.2 trades/day and has live_n=13; the two filter arms over the identical window sit at live_n=7 (vol-4x) and live_n=3 (entry-8pct), i.e. roughly 2x to 4x slower. A sub-dollar cut of unknown size — nothing in this context states how many of the 176 coins price below $1 — applied to a confirm target of n=600 against only 62.0 days of data means the realistic sample is unquantifiable in advance and plainly short of the planned n. At corrected alpha 0.00833 over 6 lifetime tests, and given the context's own statement that a fixed n=100 detects only very large effects, a tick-geometry effect that also has to clear the 0.12% extra-fill slippage haircut is exactly the small effect that requires the full planned sample the arm cannot reach. The hypothesis further confounds itself: the mechanism is claimed for coarse-grid names, but removed sub-dollar names are also where thin-alt mean reversion lives (G-41: 145 of 172 HL coins are HL-only), so a WR move would be inseparable from a universe change rather than an execution-grid change, in a single 62.0-day regime.

It will cut sample volume below the 25.0 control trades/day arrival so confirm n=600 takes longer. The arm dies if win rate is flat or lower than control, and it dies even on a win-rate lift if net EV per trade is flat or lower — that outcome means velocity is only a win-rate dial paying volume, which is precisely how G-08 died, and slower accumulation buys it no reprieve.
